concerns.text: The plan states that a paired Wilcoxon signed‑rank test will be run on the **vectors of per‑sample Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Sharpness** (see “Statistical Analysis Plan (Revised)” and the metric definition in research.md). However, ECE is defined as an **aggregate scalar** computed by binning predictions across the entire test set; it is not a per‑sample quantity. Performing a Wilcoxon test on a non‑existent per‑sample ECE vector is therefore methodologically invalid. The same issue applies to Sharpness if it is treated as a per‑sample scalar without clear definition. The analysis should instead use per‑sample, well‑defined statistics (e.g., binary coverage indicator for calibration, interval width for sharpness) or compare the aggregate scalar metrics across methods using appropriate paired tests (e.g., paired t‑test on bootstrap‑derived metric estimates).
